Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

lie verb and noun

say something untrue

also tell a lie, tell lies, a lie, lies, lying, liar, fib

classical

Hor. S. 2.6.32: nōn mentiar
Sen. Ep. 107.2: id est mentiāris
Traupman 339

mentior, mentīrī, mentītus sum

verb, fourth conjugation, deponent

lie, tell a lie

Other words

  • mendācium, mendāciī n. — a lie

    noun, second declension · classical · Plaut. Asin. 30: cavē mihi mendācī quicquam; Traupman 339; Traupman 392

    mendācī is the old genitive, as in Plautus.

  • mendāx, mendācis — lying; as a noun, a liar

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.146: mendācī hominī; Prud. Cath. 2.102: nē lingua mendāx

  • falsum, falsī n. — a falsehood, a lie

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 155

  • falsiloquus, falsiloqua, falsiloquum — lying

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 2.2.14 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 155

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Examples

  • dīc obsecrō hercle sēriō quod tē rogem, cavē mihi mendācī quicquam

    for heaven’s sake, answer me seriously what I ask you, and no lies, mindPlaut. Asin. 29–30

  • hoc juvat et mellī est, nōn mentiar

    I won’t lie: I love it, it’s honey to meHor. S. 2.6.32

  • cum mendācī hominī nē vērum quidem dīcentī crēdere soleāmus

    since we do not believe a liar even when he tells the truthCic. Div. 2.146

  • mendācium dīcere

    to tell a lieTraupman 339

See also true, truly, believe.
